name: EMOTIC (Emotion Recognition in Context)
authors_or_creators: Ronak Kosti, Jose M. Alvarez, Adria Recasens, Agata Lapedriza — Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) and MIT CSAIL
publication_venue: CVPR 2017 (initial); IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI), 2019 (extended)
num_subjects: Not identity-controlled; ~34,320 annotated person bounding boxes (subjects are not unique identities — images sourced from web/COCO/Ade20K)
label_taxonomy: mixed: 26 fine-grained discrete emotion categories (multi-label) + 3-D continuous Valence-Arousal-Dominance (VAD)
known_issues: Multi-label discrete annotations are subjective and inter-annotator agreement is moderate (each image annotated by ~3 annotators via AMT). Class imbalance is severe — categories such as 'Engagement', 'Happiness', 'Excitement' dominate, while 'Suffering', 'Embarrassment', 'Aversion' are underrepresented. Demographic bias inherited from MS-COCO and Ade20K (Western-centric scenes, skewed age/ethnicity distribution). Bounding boxes around persons can be loose; small/occluded faces are common, making face-only methods underperform. Continuous VAD labels are scaled 1-10 with annotator variance.
modality: image (RGB, person bounding box + full scene context)
annotation_method: crowdsourced (Amazon Mechanical Turk; multiple annotators per instance, aggregated)
resolution_or_fps: Variable resolution (inherited from MS-COCO, Ade20K, and Google-collected images); typical sizes range from ~300x300 up to HD
train_val_test_split: Official split: 70% train / 10% validation / 20% test, divided at the image level — approximately 17,077 train, 2,088 val, 4,389 test images (23,266 / 3,315 / 7,203 person instances depending on version)
demographic_metadata: No explicit demographic metadata; person instances span varied ages, genders, and ethnicities but distribution mirrors MS-COCO/Ade20K (Western bias, adult-skewed). No identity or fine-grained demographic labels are released.
top_sota_model: Strong baselines report mAP ~27-32% on the 26 discrete categories and VAD mean error ~0.9-1.0 (out of 10). Recent methods leveraging context-aware transformers and CLIP-based models (e.g., EmotiCon, CAER-Net, GLAMOR-Net, and CLIP-based context models) push mAP above 35% and reduce VAD error further; reported best mAP ~36-38% as of 2023-2024.
